title: Concrete Remembers
style: dark industrial electronica, cinematic darksynth, 138 bpm half-time stride, saturated detuned analog sub-bass, dry crushing kick, cavernous snare, ticking metallic percussion, cold granular pads, low intimate baritone vocal, restrained talk-singing, minor key, vast negative space, nocturnal, first vocal within seconds, compact 2:40 song, stripped bridge, short natural ending, no EDM supersaws, no orchestral crescendo
lyrics:
[Intro]

[Verse 1]
Lights out on the ninetieth floor
Nobody lives here anymore
But the stairwell hums the way you climbed
One step heavy, one step light

[Pre-Chorus]
I put my hand against the wall
It's warm, it's warm, it knew us all

[Chorus]
You walked these halls a hundred years ago
Your footsteps poured into the floor
The stone kept every word you said
It kept the shape of every door
The concrete remembers your weight
The girders remember your hand
Everything you built is still awake
Still waiting for you to stand

[Verse 2]
Rain finds the cracks you used to fill
The elevator's waiting still
A coat hook holds the shape of you
A window holds the evening blue

[Pre-Chorus]
I put my hand against the wall
It's warm, it's warm, it knew us all

[Chorus]
You walked these halls a hundred years ago
Your footsteps poured into the floor
The stone kept every word you said
It kept the shape of every door
The concrete remembers your weight
The girders remember your hand
Everything you built is still awake
Still waiting for you to stand

[Bridge]
Nothing here forgets
Nothing here forgets
Pour me in the foundation
Let me hold the next

[Final Chorus]
The concrete remembers your weight
The girders remember your hand
Everything you built is still awake
Still waiting for you to stand

[Outro]
Nothing here forgets
